How much is the Secret Buddha Garden entrance fee? | Recent reports give 100 THB per adult, paid in cash at the entrance; some sources still quote 80 THB. Jungle safari tours include the fee in their price.
Can I ride a scooter up to the Secret Buddha Garden? | Only if you are an experienced rider and the road is dry. The road is very steep and narrow with a rough final stretch, and rental scooters' brakes overheat on the way down; a 4x4 or a tour is the safer choice.
Who built the Secret Buddha Garden? | A local fruit farmer began placing sculptures on his hillside land in 1976 and kept working on it until he died in 1990. His family then opened the garden to visitors and still run it; sources differ on his name.
How long do I need at the Secret Buddha Garden? | Allow 45–60 minutes to walk the paths, see the sculptures and the stream and rest at the café, plus 30–45 minutes' drive each way from Lamai or Chaweng.
Is the Secret Buddha Garden included on the jungle safari? | Yes, it is a standard stop on the 4x4 jungle safari, usually with Na Muang waterfall, Wat Khunaram, Hin Ta and Hin Yai, lunch and the Big Buddha. The safari costs around 1,700 THB on the market and includes entry fees.
Is the Secret Buddha Garden open in the rainy season? | Yes, it is open 09:00–18:00 all year, but from October to December the road and paths are slippery and fog can close in on the hills. Go by 4x4 in wet weather, never by scooter.
What is the difference between the Secret Buddha Garden and Tarnim Magic Garden? | They are the same place. Tarnim Magic Garden is the name on many signs and maps; Secret Buddha Garden is the name most visitors and tours use.
Is the Secret Buddha Garden suitable for children? | Yes for walking children who are supervised, as the paths are short and the sculptures are fun to spot. The paths are rocky and steep in places with no railings by the stream, and it is not suitable for pushchairs.
